newsitem.title: USA: Staples lawyer defends merger from states' attack.
newsitem.headline: Staples lawyer defends merger from states' attack.

text.p: The lead attorney for the proposed merger of office superstore chains Office Depot Inc and Staples Inc on Friday defended the merger from attack by the attorneys general of eight states.
The lawyer, Don Kempf, said the state officials were wrong in arguing that the merger was "wholly at odds" with the interests of consumers and would result in higher prices.

"In this case, it is the unthinking antitrust inside-aficionados that are 'wholly at odds,' not only with sound antitrust policy but with common sense as well," Kempf told Reuters in a telephone interview.

He said the eight attorneys general had "elevated their fascination with untested new theories over the real-world reality that this merger will serve consumers well by providing them, directly, with lower prices than either Staples or Office Depot could provide on a stand-alone basis."
New York Attorney General Dennis Vacco said the merger was not in the best interests of consumers.
"My office's investigation of the proposed merger...has shown that competition between the companies results in lower prices for New York consumers," he said in a statement.
Vacco said that if the merger takes place, it "will eliminate that competition and result in higher prices and less office superstore expansion in New York."
The eight states today were filing a "friend of the court" brief with U.S. District Court Judge Thomas Hogan opposing the merger.
